title: Starter skill-bridge mini-kanban: 14d checklist and interview memos
content:
Purpose and scope:
A lightweight, repeatable 14-day skill-bridge mini-kanban designed for fast contractor -> IC conversion and for rapid first-release readiness for new hires. This is intentionally low-friction: mix of checklists, short interview-evidence capture prompts, and handoff scripts for hiring managers and mentors.

Why we made this:
- Avoid long-form onboarding decks when problem is tight scope delivery (bug fix / small feature).
- Create consistent evidence artifacts for hiring conversion decisions so judgement is reproducible.
- Keep managers accountable with clear micro-deadlines over first 14 days.

How to use this doc (notes to self):
- Copy kanban columns into a new Jira or Linear board (tag with "skill-bridge/<name>").
- Use interview-evidence snippets in async debriefs when candidate finishes day 7 checkpoint.
- This is intentionally permissive; adapt to pool size 1-3 hires.

Kanban columns (14-day cadence):
1) Pre-Start (owner: People Ops)
   - Accesses created: laptop, corp VPN, GH ro/team, CI read, Slack (confirm by day -1)
   - Intro packet sent: key repos, CODEOWNERS, runbook link
   - Buddy assigned and calendar blocks set (30m/day first 7 days)
2) Day 0-3 (owner: Manager + Buddy)
   - Quick env smoke test: build + run local dev server (checkbox)
   - Small runnable task created: "hello-world change" with PR template
   - 30m sync: expectations & 2-week plan
   - Evidence capture: paste PR link and 3-line note: "completed dev env, made PR X with Y obstacles"
3) Day 4-7 (owner: Buddy)
   - Feature task: non-blocking ticket that touches product boundary
   - Shadow oncall rotation: read-runbook + 1 pager on incident flow (if applicable)
   - Async interview: buddy posts short writeup in hiring-thread (see template below)
   - 1-week checkpoint meeting scheduled (manager + candidate + buddy)
4) Day 8-12 (owner: Manager)
   - Ramp task: independent small feature or bug with hotfix potential
   - Code review behavior: quality, responses, and remediation speed captured
   - Pairing sessions: 2 x 45m with different teammates
   - Candidate fills short self-eval form (link to HR-4823)
5) Day 13-14 (owner: Manager + People Ops)
   - Final conversion review packet prepared (see rubric)
   - Manager recommendation sent to People Ops + evidence bundle
   - Handoff: if converting, create permanent role invite and 30-60-90 plan

Interview-evidence capture template (paste into thread or ticket):
- Candidate name: 
- Role applied/converted to: 
- Summary (2 lines): what they accomplished this sprint
- Strengths observed (3 bullets)
- Risks / concerns (3 bullets)
- Code sample links (PRs/commits): list
- Oncall/readiness notes: yes/no + short detail
- Quick score: Tech(1-5), Ownership(1-5), Communication(1-5)
- Recommendation: convert / extend trial / decline

Scoring rubric (used for final packet):
- Tech correctness (1-5): adherence to architecture, tests, edge cases
- Speed to impact (1-5): how quickly they shipped working code
- Collaboration (1-5): responsiveness in reviews, pair sessions
- Learning curve (1-5): how they adapted to new systems and feedback
- Final guidance: total >= 16 -> recommend conversion; 12-15 -> extend trial 14 days; <12 -> decline or reassign

Manager checklist for conversion packet (deliverables):
- 1-week checkpoint notes and midterm PR links
- Final PR(s) showing independent code with at least one approved review
- Buddy writeup (2 paragraphs) and paired session notes
- Candidate self-eval (1 paragraph on biggest challenge and next steps)
- Manager recommendation email body (template below)

Manager recommendation email template (copy/paste):
Subject: Conversion recommendation: [Name] -> [Role]
Body: Short context (2 lines) + evidence bullets (3) + recommendation (convert / extend / decline) + next-step ask to People Ops (onboarding admin, payroll triggers, hardware order)

Common risk signals (callout):
- Repeated inability to run local tests after 3 days without a plan
- PR churn: >4 force-pushes without reviewer learning note
- Communication gaps: missed paired sessions or no async updates
- Security/access issues: sensitive repo access misuse or unclear handling of secrets

Lightweight oncall/incident readiness (if role requires):
- Day 4: read incidents runbook + sign acknowledgment
- Day 7: walk through a postmortem with buddy
- Evidence: link to a short note "walked incident X, understood triage"

Slack templates (use for structured async signals):
- Day 3 update (buddy -> people-ops): "DAY3 CHECK: [Name] env ok; PR 12 open; needs input on infra token; recommend keep pacing."
- Week1 recap (manager thread): paste evidence template + short rec

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Should we enforce mandatory automated tests on Day 7 PR? (pros/cons)
- How many conversions per quarter can manager-run pipeline support before People Ops steps in? (ops capacity planning)
- Decide template storage: Confluence HR page or a new tiny repo with templates. Confluence link above for current working copy.

Appendix: examples and links used in practice (replace with project specifics):
- Example PR: PR-gh/infra/567
- Example Jira board prefix: SB- (skill-bridge)
- Candidate self-eval quick form: https://forms.redwood.ai/short-self-eval

Final note (voice, informal):
This is intentionally a compact kit — treat it as a living checklist. We want low cognitive load for managers and fast reproducible evidence for fair conversions. Repeat after me: "evidence beats impressions".

Last edited by: Asha Menon (people-ops).
